card.title: One-Act Play 1 — A Matter of Husbands (Ferenc Molnár)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The play at a glance "A Matter of Husbands" by Ferenc Molnár is a one-act comedy of verbal judo: the Earnest Woman arrives at the Famous Actress's dressing room accusing her of stealing her husband — a dramatist who writes the actress's plays — and the actress, without denying anything at first, talks her out of the accusation entirely by inventing a better story: the husband never had an affair; he invented one…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Farce about jealousy: the wife suspects a stage actor, the husband deflects cleverly.
Comedy of misunderstanding — trace how the playwright resolves it without proof.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: Gender role reversal: the wife outwits the powerful manager — state the reversal as the feminist reading.  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **The Famous Actress** is the play's mind: intelligent, theatrical, entirely unscrupulous — and her skill is precisely the point, since the play asks whether a better story beats a true one. Her performance within the performance is the play's engine, and Molnár gives her the best of every exchange.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **The power of narrative over fact** — the central theme: the wife has evidence and loses; the actress has a story and wins; the play is an experiment in which fiction defeats reality in a fair fight. **Theatre and deception** — the actress's profession is her weapon: the theme that the skills of performance do not stay on stage.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. Why does the Earnest Woman visit the Famous Actress? (2 marks)** A. To confront her over an affair with her husband — a dramatist who writes the actress's plays — armed with the evidence of absences and notes. She arrives expecting a rival and meets, instead, a storyteller. **Q. How does the Actress explain the husband's behaviour? (2 marks)** A.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. How does the actress win her argument with her husband? (2 marks) — she pretends a role would force a kiss scene, then reveals it was a ruse to test him.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "The Actress wins not by denying the truth but by retelling it." Discuss the strategy and its significance. (8 marks)** A model answer analyses the strategy step by step: denial would invite testing, so the actress reclassifies — converting evidence into art, suspicion into research, betrayal into a playwright's method — and performs the innocent intermediary with all her…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The action, scene by scene The setup is a confrontation: the Earnest Woman, ordinary, anxious, armed with evidence — her husband's absences, the notes, the suspicion — arrives at the actress's dressing room to demand the truth. Molnár stages the mismatch from the first minute: the wife has reality on her side; the actress has narrative.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Dramatic irony** — the play's master device: the audience watches the actress lie and the wife believe, holding the truth the characters on stage cannot; every comforting sentence the wife receives is a sentence the audience knows to be false. - **The story-within-the-story** — the actress's invention: an affair reclassified as a playwright's research.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: The play satirises theatrical life: an actress manipulates her manager-husband by inventing a romantic role for 'Paula' — the manipulation IS the comedy; explain the trick.  ·  Trick 2: The unseen 'Paula' is the device: she exists only in the wife's story — analyse how an absent character drives the plot.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What is humorous about the manager's reaction? (2 marks) — the shrewd businessman is completely out-manoeuvred by his wife's invention.
